item.title: AI microdramas cause ‘aesthetic fatigue’, professor tells Macau forum
item.description: Formulaic AI-generated microdramas risk stifling human creativity and innovation, a Beijing professor has warned at a forum in Macau. Zhang Lanshan, a professor at the School of Digital Media and Design Arts at the Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said that while audiences loved such standardised content, it posed a risk to diversity and artistic endeavour. item.title: Alibaba chip unit T-Head files Hong Kong IPO plan amid China’s AI self-sufficiency drive
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding’s chip design unit T-Head has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) on a confidential basis in Hong Kong, the company said in a stock-exchange filing on Tuesday evening, setting up a high-profile listing in the city amid rising competition between the US and China as the latter continues its push for tech self-sufficiency. item.title: Operation Santa Claus launched in Hong Kong to bring care to ‘every corner of the city’
item.description: Operation Santa Claus (OSC), one of Hong Kong’s most enduring annual fundraising campaigns, has been launched, with organisers aiming to raise money for 13 local charities this year to “bring care and hope to every corner of the city”. During the launch ceremony on Tuesday, co-organisers RTHK and the South China Morning Post said they would continue the campaign’s decades-long mission of uniting Hong Kong’s communities to support those most in need. item.title: Abby Choi’s ex-brother-in-law tells court he had ‘a rather special existence’

item.title: Data link trial: Chinese team finds hollow-core fibre cuts lag 30% across 1,000km
item.description: Light travels through conventional optical fibres at about 200,000km per second – about two-thirds the speed it travels in a vacuum – because the signals are passing through solid glass. When vast amounts of data are exchanged between computing centres hundreds or thousands of kilometres apart, this difference amounts to a substantial delay.
